gen_risks.description: Regional instability and ongoing conflict in South Sudan could cause further refugee influxes, straining public services and water infrastructure in host communities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide dedicated financing for refugee-hosting districts to construct sustainable piped water systems and establish close coordination mechanisms with UNHCR and OPM.
gen_risks.evidence: The most critical risk to this outlook is regional instability, particularly from the ongoing conflict in South Sudan.

gen_risks.description: Climate variability, extreme temperatures, and intense precipitation events may cause severe flooding or dry spells, damaging water infrastructure and disrupting supply.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate climate resilience into design standards, implement catchment management measures, protect buffer zones, and reforest riverine areas.
gen_risks.evidence: increased temperatures would produce higher levels of potential evapotranspiration... climate change is expected to result in more intense precipitation

gen_risks.description: Low dry-season water flows at the Namatala River intake in Mbale may fail to meet projected water demand while maintaining mandatory environmental flows.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct an Augmented Water Supply Study to evaluate water impoundment, borehole additions, source expansion, and managed demand reduction during dry spells.
gen_risks.evidence: Namatala’s dry weather flows in some cases may not be sufficient to meet projected water demand and maintain an adequate EF.

gen_risks.description: Limited staff capacity and lack of familiarity with World Bank procurement regulations in the Procurement Disposal Units may cause procurement delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit experienced procurement consultants to support the PST, provide specialized training on the New Procurement Framework, and establish payment tracking.
gen_risks.evidence: PDU staff requirement of additional training on World Bank Procurement Regulations and Procedures; inefficiency in processing, causing delays

gen_risks.description: Incomplete needs assessments and insufficient geotechnical studies during design phase could lead to frequent contract variations, design changes, and cost/time overruns.
gen_risks.mitigation: Require detailed engineering designs and complete geotechnical assessments upfront, and mandate formal contract management plans before contract execution.
gen_risks.evidence: incomplete needs assessments and inadequate attention to geotechnical studies leading to design changes/variations during implementation

gen_risks.description: Incomplete operationalization of the project module within the MWE's Integrated Financial Management System (IFMS) creates risks of financial reporting errors.
gen_risks.mitigation: Fully operationalize the IFMS project module at MWE, retain qualified financial management specialists, and ensure regular internal audit reporting.
gen_risks.evidence: the project module of the IFMS has not been fully operationalized at the MWE, which increases the risk of errors and inaccuracy

gen_risks.description: Umbrella Water Authorities (UWAs) managing small town schemes may fail to achieve full cost recovery, leaving them reliant on public subsidies for capital investments.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish tariff guidelines ensuring full O&M cost coverage plus a 25% margin, enforce automatic tariff adjustments, and contract professional management firms.
gen_risks.evidence: While the UWAs can cover their routine O&M costs, they are still dependent on public financing for capital investments

gen_risks.description: Inadequate coordination between humanitarian agencies, local authorities, and national ministries risks improper borehole siting near pit latrines, causing groundwater contamination.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish multi-stakeholder coordination mechanisms across MWE, OPM, UNHCR, and local governments, and apply standard water source protection distance rules.
gen_risks.evidence: lack of coordination resulted in boreholes being drilled too close to each other or too close to shallow pit latrines, risking contamination

gen_risks.description: Influx of external construction workers into local communities may lead to social tensions, gender-based violence, sexual exploitation, and disease transmission.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce mandatory contractor worker codes of conduct, prioritize local hiring, separate worker camps from local settlements, and conduct community sensitization.
gen_risks.evidence: social misdemeanor by workers (labor influx)... GBV, such as sexual assaults of women and girls

gen_risks.description: Land acquisition and right-of-way requirements for water supply networks and treatment facilities may cause involuntary resettlement, loss of assets, and execution delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement approved Resettlement Policy Frameworks and site-specific RAPs, provide timely compensation, and establish dedicated project grievance redress mechanisms.
gen_risks.evidence: potential negative social impacts that might result from the need for land acquisition and/or the loss of access to economic assets and livelihoods

gen_risks.description: Inadequately managed effluent discharge from fecal sludge treatment facilities (FSTFs) into receiving watercourses could cause stream eutrophication and health hazards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Design FSTFs with percolate treatment systems, conduct regular effluent quality monitoring, install warning signage, and provide safe alternative drinking water.
gen_risks.evidence: potential of eutrophication in the FSTF receiving stream (i.e., Okame stream) if the discharge effluent is not adequately managed

gen_risks.description: Improper handling, removal, and disposal of legacy Asbestos Cement (AC) pipes during pipe replacement works creates severe occupational health and environmental hazards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and enforce specific asbestos waste management procedures following NEMA guidelines, providing safe handling, packaging, transport, and disposal.
gen_risks.evidence: improper handling of asbestos cement (AC) pipes, OHS risks

gen_risks.description: Prolonged internal approval processes at MWE cause delays in paying vendors, resulting in cash flow disruptions for contractors and slower construction progress.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish an automated payment tracking system, streamline internal sign-off procedures, and enforce strict approval timelines across departments.
gen_risks.evidence: delays in paying vendors due to prolonged internal approval processes.

gen_risks.description: Limited capacity among domestic contractors to execute complex water infrastructure contracts may result in low bidding competition or reliance on international contractors.
gen_risks.mitigation: Package contracts to match market capacity, conduct market sounding, encourage joint ventures with domestic firms, and allow adequate mobilization time.
gen_risks.evidence: limited capacity of domestic contractors to conduct projects of this nature, complexity, and scope

gen_risks.description: Over-pumping or localized depletion of aquifers supplying solar-powered piped water schemes could threaten the long-term sustainability of groundwater sources.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct a national groundwater assessment, perform detailed yield and drawdown studies prior to drilling, and establish an operational groundwater monitoring toolkit.
gen_risks.evidence: Despite Uganda’s growing dependency on groundwater, concerns remain over its sustainability.

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk: as detailed in the CPF, significant political uncertainty is not foreseen, but governance and effective public-sector management present substantial risks.
gt_risks.mitigation: The Project will mitigate these risks through (a) strengthening the MWE's regulatory framework; (b) carrying out a citizen engagement strategy; and (c) strengthening project implementation efforts in close coordination with local government officials and development partners. The World Bank's procurement processes will also help safeguard the Project from corruption.

gt_risks.description: Institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability risk: the Umbrella Water Authority (UWA) as a regional service delivery model for small towns and RGCs was recently introduced. Although the decision to scale up this model was informed by extensive analytical work and a pilot project, the UWA model was only recently operationalized.
gt_risks.mitigation: The Project will support implementation of a professionalized monitoring system focused on enhancing revenue collection approaches (billing software, cashless/mobile payment systems) and on strengthening integration of specialized private operators through improved contract management. The implementation team will use the Utility Performance Monitoring and Information System (UPMIS) tool to regularly review UWA and NWSC performance.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk: the Procurement risk is rated Substantial while the FM risk is Moderate. The risks identified relate to delays and skills gaps at different stages of procurement processing.
gt_risks.mitigation: IWMDP will benefit from the lessons learned and mechanisms put in place under the predecessor project (WMDP); detailed mitigation measures for the procurement risk are set out in the Appraisal (Procurement) section.

gt_risks.description: The environmental and social risk is deemed Substantial given (a) potential opposition to the introduction of a new service delivery model, including new tariffs and catchment management measures; (b) the influx of new workers in small towns and RGCs; and (c) potentially adverse environmental impacts from the construction and operation of the proposed investments.
gt_risks.mitigation: The environmental and social risk will be managed through the application of an Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF), a Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF), and related safeguards instruments (Environmental and Social Impact Assessment, Resettlement Action Plans).

gt_risks.description: Other risks (social tensions in districts hosting refugees): tensions between refugees and citizens are caused by inequity in access to and payment for water supply and sanitation (WSS) services. While refugees in the settlements benefit from humanitarian aid and GoU support, Ugandans in host communities receive limited support for services and infrastructure, causing social tension that may result in Project implementation delays given potential community opposition to the works.
gt_risks.mitigation: The GoU has prioritized development efforts for poor districts hosting refugees while remaining firmly committed to its policy on refugee protection. The Project will manage this risk by designing WSS facilities and catchment management measures that benefit both host communities and refugees, and by ensuring the Project's social and communication management plan is applied and adequately supervised. There are no known existing risks to the refugee protection framework or reputational risks for the Project.
